_readme: Every slide of every slider on the site, in one place, so the copy and the
media can be edited without touching component code and can later be served
by a CMS instead of this file. `src/lib/slides-content.ts` is the only module
that reads it; the carousel modules re-export from there, so the shape below
is the contract a CMS has to produce.
`framing` describes how a photo sits inside its frame. Two rules come from
the designers' prototype and are the only per-image treatments in it:
- destinations photos: centred in desktop_v8, bottom-anchored in v9 (the
full-bleed crop is taller, so the subject has to hold the lower edge).
That one is variant-wide, so it lives in the slider's `framing`.
- privateWorld card 0: scaled 1.1 from its bottom-left corner, identical
in both builds. That one is per-slide.
The prototype ships no per-width image sources (no srcset, no <picture>, no
media-query background swaps) — what changes with width is the frame, not
the file. Those frame rules are CSS and live with the sections.

copy.title: Utopia - Jericoacoara
copy.description: Brazil's ultimate kitesurfing mecca. Where dramatic white dunes meet an unmatched, laid-back vibe.

_mediaNote: Two crops of the same three shots, one per layout tier — this is the
one slider where the prototype really does ship per-width sources.
`video`/`poster` are the PORTRAIT cut the mobile builds use (v3 and
v9-mobile: assets/kitesurf.mp4, dunes.mp4, localvibes.mp4 — ours are
byte-identical to theirs, under opt/). `videoWide`/`posterWide` are the
LANDSCAPE cut desktop_v8/v9/v10 use for the same slides (their
fullwidth__bg-video, again byte-identical to ours under desktop/).
Verified frame by frame, not by filename — the names do not line up:
the designers' `fullwidth-birds` IS our `localvibes` slide (the scarlet
ibis over the dunes), which is why the third entry pairs them.
webm leads on desktop because the prototype's <source> order does:
the VP9 cut is 2.7/3.3/5.4 MB against 14.0/9.6/10.6 for the H.264 one.
That is only true of desktop/fullwidth-*.webm. Do NOT reinstate
/assets/opt/kitesurf.webm — it is an older edit of the kitesurf shot
(the kite enters from the opposite side), so webm-capable browsers
would silently play the wrong cut.
The -mobile / .hevc encodes the component derives from `video` are
ours, not the designers': the mobile builds serve the full 5.8 MB

_framingNote: The cards are centred: desktop_v8/v9 set `object-position: 50% 50%` on
all three (`.pw-card[data-index=N] img`) and Figma 24.07 draws the
mobile active card centred too (`154:6319` overhangs its 276x366 frame
by 8.9 left and 13.4 top, i.e. half the overflow on each axis). The
earlier `center 35%` came from the *mobile* prototype v3
(`.days__card img` in v3/css/sections.css) and rode over every width,
which is what pushed the crop toward the top of the photo.
Figma's two desktop cards sit ~12px lower still (`154:4229` 386x540 at
y=-24 and `154:4232` 308x431 at y=-19 are bottom-anchored, both a 4.65%
overflow), but the third (`154:4234`) is top-anchored, so the frames are
eyeballed rather than a rule — the prototype's 50% is the rule.
desktop_v8/v9 also crop card 0 with `scale(1.1)` from its bottom-left corner
(`.pw-card[data-index="0"] img`). That correction belongs to THEIR asset:
their pw-1.jpg is 1782x2383, ours is a tighter 1696x2528 crop of the same
photograph, so our frame already shows what their 1.1 zoom produces.
Cards 1 and 2 use byte-identical files and need no correction.
Applying the rule here would double the zoom — left neutral on purpose.
